Aisha (PM): quick huddle: we have two competing slips for the June ship — multi-tenant embeddings cache (high perf + risky infra work) vs. prompt-templating (UX polish). ACME pilot is pushing for embeddings. Need a call: ship embeddings in a limited form + cut templating, or postpone embeddings and keep templating? thoughts?
Ravi (Eng): short: cache work hits an unknown KV bug under long sequences. Full multi-tenant cache needs deeper infra changes and a few perf patches. That said, we can ship a stripped-down embeddings path that does no kv-cache (stateless lookup) and enforce strict rate limits. Engineering estimate: stripped path = 4 dev days + monitoring; full cache = 10+ dev days + infra churn.
Lena (ML): on eval side, stripped (no cache) has slightly worse tail latency and 6% lower semantic recall vs full cache, but still acceptable for pilot customers. If ACME runs it, they should expect lower throughput and occasional higher latency.
Noah (Design): templating removes friction and reduces prompt errors, but it's not blocking for initial customers. It improves onboarding time, though. If we axe it, we should make the prompt examples more obvious in the UI.
Priya (CS): ACME wants embeddings in some form or they pause pilot. They said they'd accept a "limited-lane" offering (invite-only, quotas). They also asked for a clear rollback plan and a feedback loop.
Aisha (PM): reframe options: 1) ship stripped embeddings globally + cut prompt-templating (fastest to market, risk: cost & perf), 2) pilot-lane embeddings (invited customers on dedicated pool) + keep templating (safer but delays wider availability), 3) drop embeddings from MVP and ship templating. Which balances launch and customer commitments?
Ravi (Eng): lean to option 1 if we can gate by default and have hard rate limits (to avoid cost blowouts). It's less infra work than full cache and keeps us from landing risky infra changes.
Lena (ML): option1 ok, but we need acceptance tests and a rollout plan to track semantic quality and P95 latency. I can add continuous eval checks.
Noah (Design): option1 means we lose templating polish. I can create a compact prompt-form that reduces error for MVP in ~2 dev days of frontend work — acceptable trade.
Priya (CS): ACME likes option2 but will tolerate option1 if we get them a clear SLA and an onboarding session. They prefer "invite-only" but will accept global with quota if docs + support are good.
Aisha (PM): voting: 1=striped embeddings global + cut templating, 2=pilot-lane embeddings + keep templating, 3=drop embeddings ship templating
Ravi (Eng): 1
Lena (ML): 1 (but with eval hooks)
Noah (Design): 1 (I can deliver the compact prompt UI)
Priya (CS): 2 but will accept 1 if SLA and support are documented
Aisha (PM): consensus = 1 with conditions: a) default rate limits applied to embeddings endpoints b) monitoring/alerts for latency + recall c) customer-facing note + onboarding for ACME d) prompt-templating deprioritized to post-MVP. Action list: @Ravi implement rate limits + stripped embeddings path; @Ravi open infra ticket for emergency rollback toggle; @Lena add continuous recall eval & probes; @Noah ship compact prompt examples and quick-start; @Priya schedule ACME onboarding + draft SLA.
deploy-bot: created feature-flag rollout/embeddings-stripped (staged=false)
Ravi (Eng): opened ticket INFRA-2044 for rollback toggle and rate-limit config. PR for stripped embeddings path is WIP.
Lena (ML): added eval job to CI and a dashboard widget (link: https://dash.rwd/embeds-recall)
Noah (Design): uploaded compact prompt kit to driveshare: https://rwd.example/compact-prompts
Priya (CS): emailed ACME with proposed plan + tentative SLA. They requested a 30-min onboarding call.
Aisha (PM): I'll update the release tracker: "MVP decision: ship stripped (non-cached) embeddings with strict rate limits; delay multi-tenant embeddings cache to v1; deprioritize prompt-templating to post-MVP. Monitoring + rollback guard required for launch." Tagging @launch-team. Keep updates in this thread. :+1:
